newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dlr ends at 8-yr low as downtrend resumes.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dlr ends at 8-yr low as downtrend resumes.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed at an eight-year low against its U.S. counterpart on Wednesday amid growing anticipation that a slow 1997 depreciation was resuming, dealers said.
The local unit dipped as low as T$27.935 before closing at T$27.926 against Tuesday's T$27.921 finish, marking its lowest level since closing at T$28.03 on January 7, 1989.
Wednesday's T$27.926 close surpassed the previous eight-year low of T$27.921 set on Tuesday.
Turnover through dealers was an active US$231.5 million.
Dealers attributed the Taiwan dollar fall mainly to actual commercial greenback demand from importers and individuals.
They said they central bank had entered to keep the Taiwan dollar from falling too sharply, but intervention was limited.
"The central bank did not staunchly stop the Taiwan dollar depreciation," said one dealer. "It simply tried to smooth the fall because there was actual U.S. dollar demand today."
Dealers said the Taiwan dollar depreciation would help the island's exports, a trend that even the central bank would not find unwelcome as long as it is not precipitous.

"As long as there is actual greenback demand -- not speculation -- and the degree of decline is not too large, the central bank, I believe, will not try to stop it (the depreciation)," said another dealer.

Dealers said they saw little speculation on Wednesday, in contrast to late Monday and Tuesday, when overseas interests were seen testing the central bank's defence levels through non-delivery forward buying.

Taiwan's currency has been on a slow decline since early 1997, with senior analysts polled by Reuters forecasting that the rate would slip to T$28 to the U.S. dollar in the second half -- but only when the central bank is ready.
"The Taiwan dollar likely will test T$28 soon," said the first dealer.
A T$27.90-95 range was seen for Thursday.
